text.tspan: Everyday English - B1 - 2026/07/10 - Essay - 01
Readers spend time with books.
Pexels · 6344242
A little time to read
There is more than one way to read a short book. In my experience, practical preparation and attention to others are two useful
starting points.
One reason is that a small reading goal is easier to keep than an ambitious one. For instance, we read five pages after lunch rather
than wait for a free afternoon. This prevents a small difficulty from taking over the experience. It also leaves us more time to notice
what is happening.
Another reason is that discussing an idea helps us understand it more clearly. For example, we explain a favourite passage to a
friend and listen to a different interpretation. This approach recognises that the experience belongs to more than one person and that
different people may need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control every detail. We can make a
sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the conclusion. Each
body paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the argument rather than introduce a
new proposal.
Write about an attempt to read a short book that did not go as planned. Explain two lessons, each supported by a specific incident.
Use four short paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One possible outline: introduce the situation;
discuss a small reading goal is easier to keep than an ambitious one with an example; discuss discussing an idea helps us
understand it more clearly with a different example; conclude by connecting the two points.)
